clue.text: Stocky rednecks entertained by festival

indicators.note: the rednecks are entertained, held as guests, inside the festival word

parts.note: Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival
hicks are unsophisticated rural folk, like rednecks

explanation.surface: Burly country types are being hosted at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: TET, the Vietnamese lunar new year, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset describes a heavily built, solid body, which is what stocky means.

clue.text: An idiot cycling with Alf

indicators.note: cycling means letters go round, moving from the front of the phrase with Alf to its back

explanation.surface: Someone foolish going on a bike ride with a friend called Alf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves WIT from the front of WITHALF to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfwit is a common insulting word for a foolish or stupid person.

clue.text: Records collection chef keeps while first in England and Belgium

indicators.note: the chef word keeps, holds, the other letters within it

parts.note: a chef is a cook
as can mean while, at the same time that

indicators.note: first in takes the opening letter of England

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A cook holds onto something while working in England and Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first in' applies to England for E; Belgium gives its abbreviation B.
explanation.definitionFit: A casebook is a collection of records of cases, as kept by a doctor or detective.

clue.text: Boss with yen for learning

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud on a surface
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency yen

explanation.surface: A manager with a hunger for education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is not an employer here but a decorative knob.
explanation.definitionFit: Study is the activity of acquiring knowledge, the same as learning.

clue.text: Experimental musical mounted under marquee for example

indicators.note: in a down clue the later piece sits under the earlier one

parts.note: a marquee is a large kind of tent

indicators.note: mounted means put upwards, so in this down entry the musical title is written bottom to top

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A trial theatre show staged under a big tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns EVITA into ATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tentative is provisional, done as a trial, hence experimental.

clue.text: Note 27's come round again

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
27 across is HOUND, and a cur is a hound

explanation.surface: A musical note's dog comes back round.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends the solver to 27 across, HOUND, a synonym of CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen or appear again, coming round once more.

clue.text: True when at sea with navy a volley possibly needed

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of true are mixed up

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Something true while sailing with the navy, when a burst of gunfire is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a volley' suggests naval gunfire, but it is a tennis shot.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a volley is one kind of return, hitting the ball back before it bounces.

clue.text: Wheel around in short coat in a circle of flowers

indicators.note: in places the wheel word inside the shortened coat
short means the coat word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as the word itself before trimming
to wheel around is to roll

explanation.surface: Turning in a small jacket within a ring of blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the last letter of the coat word, leaving COA, as in a cropped jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: The corolla is the ring of petals of a flower, a botanical term.

clue.text: Moves queen up — vulnerable castle takes nothing

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the queen letters are written bottom to top

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a regular abbreviation for queen

indicators.note: vulnerable suggests something broken open, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A chess commentary: the queen advances while a weak rook takes no pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ER into RE; 'vulnerable' mixes CASTLE with O into LOCATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To relocate is to move to a new place, so relocates means moves.

clue.text: Special gin in cocktail? This might be a plus

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed

explanation.surface: A special gin in a mixed drink could be a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in cocktail' mixes GIN into IGN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is one example of a mathematical sign, as is a minus.

clue.text: Does no work — did less after blowing cover

indicators.note: blowing cover means losing the outer letters, leaving the inside of did less

explanation.surface: Someone slacks off: they did less after their cover was blown.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to be inactive, so idles means is not working.

clue.text: Unfortunately annual rut is affected

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deer's yearly mating season unluckily is disrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected behaviour is put on or artificial, the opposite of natural.

clue.text: He might deliver latest in the Dow Jones branch office in the City

indicators.note: latest means the final letters of in, the, Dow and Jones

parts.note: BO is an abbreviation for branch office

indicators.note: in the City read as the last letter in the word City

explanation.surface: A financial courier brings the Dow Jones news to a branch in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, fitting the Dow Jones surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsboy is a boy who delivers or sells newspapers.

clue.text: A medium seeing adventurous girl almost restraining sob

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the girl's name holds the sob word inside
almost means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Alice has adventures in Wonderland
to cry is to sob

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant consulted by a daring girl who is nearly in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A medium' suggests a psychic; it is an artist's paint. The adventurous girl is Alice of Wonderland, and 'almost' leaves ALIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic paint is a medium artists work in, alongside oils and watercolour.

clue.text: Concerned with virus? A way to turn back NICE elaborated

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: back means the word for to turn is read in reverse

parts.note: to go is to have a turn, as in a game

indicators.note: elaborated means worked out in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sounds like advice to the health watchdog NICE on handling a virus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GO into OG; 'elaborated' turns NICE into ENIC. NICE is the UK body that rules on medical treatments.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathogenic means disease-causing, the property of a virus or germ.

clue.text: Hammer raised while I finish off bloodsucker like a vampire

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means the hammer word is written upwards

parts.note: to rap is to hammer or knock
as can mean while

indicators.note: finish off means the bloodsucker word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tick is a bloodsucking parasite

explanation.surface: A hammer raised to finish off a vampire, stake in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns RAP into PAR; 'finish off' trims TICK to TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Parasitic means living off another's blood or body, as a vampire does.

clue.text: Terminus very large to manage — this allows an internal review

parts.note: a terminus is an end
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: A huge railway terminus to run, with an internal inspection needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internal review' suggests an office audit, but it means looking inside the body.
explanation.definitionFit: An endoscope is a medical instrument for viewing the inside of the body.

clue.text: Final thing to make shoe

definitions.meaning: a cobbler's foot-shaped model on which a shoe is made

explanation.definitionFit: Last means final, and is also the cobbler's model for shaping footwear.

clue.text: For couples a tango's a pain in Torremolinos on vacation

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in puts the pain word inside the emptied resort name
on vacation means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of Torremolinos

parts.note: an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: For pairs of dancers, a tango is agony on a Spanish holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties Torremolinos, keeping only its first and last letters; 'couples' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach is to join one thing to another, so attaches means couples.

clue.text: Resistance/current gradient?

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance
the amp is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Looks like an electrical formula: resistance over current, a gradient.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash between Resistance and current reads as division, but it only joins two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is a sloping surface, so it has a gradient.

clue.text: Chronicles of Midsomer unusual with no dead

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are arranged in an unusual way

parts.note: D is an abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Midsomer unusually has no deaths, as in the TV series Midsomer Murders, famous for its body count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes D from MIDSOMER before 'unusual' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoirs are written accounts of one's life, personal chronicles.

clue.text: Time before Xmas that's sure to broadcast exciting stories

parts.note: Advent is the church season before Christmas

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter, so the letters of sure are scattered

explanation.surface: December programmers certain to air thrilling tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to broadcast' mixes SURE into URES.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventures are tales of daring exploits, or the exploits themselves.

clue.text: One delivering frightful curse runs after earl

indicators.note: after places the runs letter behind the earl letter
frightful suggests something mangled, so the letters of curse are jumbled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone uttering a terrible curse chases after a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightful' rearranges CURSE into RESCU.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer delivers people from danger, delivering in the sense of saving.

clue.text: Dale and Virginia shout up

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the shout word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to yell is to shout

explanation.surface: Two people, Dale and Virginia, shouting loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dale' looks like a name; it is the definition, a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A dale is a valley, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Primates etc intend to reflect when caught in moral lapses

indicators.note: caught in means the intend word is held inside the lapses word

parts.note: sins are moral lapses

indicators.note: to reflect means to mirror, so the word for intend is read in reverse

parts.note: to aim is to intend

explanation.surface: Primates and others mean to think about their moral failings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflect' looks like pondering, but it signals a mirror image of the intend word, giving MIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Simians are monkeys and apes, members of the primate order.

clue.text: Relatively rare argon put in high pressures certainly having leaked

indicators.note: put in means the argon letters are placed inside the rest
high means drunk, so the remaining letters are reeling
having leaked means the certainly word has escaped from pressures

parts.note: sure means certainly
Ar is the chemical symbol for argon

explanation.surface: A rare gas fed into high-pressure containers that have definitely sprung a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having leaked' leaves PRESS; 'high' (drunk) jumbles that into SPSER around the argon symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparser means more thinly spread, so comparatively scarce or rare.

clue.text: South American greeting snack food

parts.note: US means American
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A South American welcome snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one phrase, but splits into S and US.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is Japanese vinegared rice with fish, eaten as a snack or light meal.

clue.text: Free European travel

parts.note: to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Free European train travel.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to travel on a vehicle or animal.

clue.text: Pipe charged particles in huge numbers

parts.note: to pipe is to sing in a high warbling voice, to trill
ions are electrically charged particles

explanation.surface: A tube channels vast quantities of charged particles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' suggests a tube, but here it is a bird's singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trillion is a million million, so trillions are enormous quantities.

clue.text: Part of pack to turn alternately into hearts and diamonds

indicators.note: into places the picked letters inside the card-suit letters

parts.note: H is the card abbreviation for hearts
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: alternately takes every other letter of to turn

explanation.surface: Instructions for turning a pack of cards into hearts and diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of pack' suggests a card pack; it is a hunting pack.
explanation.definitionFit: A hound is one of the dogs that make up a hunting pack.

clue.text: Copper's timid and not dangerous

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
shy means timid

explanation.surface: A police officer is nervous and harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job is easy and comfortable, posing no risk or hardship.

clue.text: Spy master is years in disguise

indicators.note: something in disguise has its appearance changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spymaster has spent years disguised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spy master' looks like one word; Spy is the definition and master gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an agent sent on a mission, sometimes a secret one, like a spy.
